nws.synopsis: Weak offshore flow will continue into Sunday. Gradual warming expected into Monday, then gradually cooler for the middle of next week with a chance of precipitation for late next week. Tides will remain elevated through much of next week.
systems: At 11 AM, the pressure gradient from San Diego to Tonopah, NV was running 5.6 mb offshore.
Weak offshore flow will continue into Sunday, becoming weakly onshore by Monday.
Given the unsettled weather quickly turning to offshore flow, marine layer low clouds and fog will be absent from the coast this weekend.

nws.aviation: 241730Z...Generally VFR conditions across the region through the period. N/NE winds strengthen through (and south of) the Cajon Pass and along south-facing mountain slopes with gusts 20-35 kts through early this afternoon. Winds weaken and eventually diminish late this afternoon and evening, but will remain weakly offshore, enough to keep most if not all low clouds from forming. 10% or less chance for cigs vcnty KSAN.

sites.name: Little Black
sites.note: Best post-frontal site in the county. West-facing, so offshore mornings are over the back.

sites.name: Blossom Valley
sites.note: Inland thermal site; often lines up with Elsinore.

sites.name: Elsinore (E / Edwards)
sites.note: East-facing over the lake; its own animal. The sea-breeze convergence line is the XC engine.

sites.name: Torrey Pines
sites.note: Ridge soaring in a steady W to WNW sea breeze. SW or NW is cross (soarable but not great); only east is over the back. Rare thermal days (1,200 ft+) are flagged as a Thermal day.

sites.name: Laguna / Horse
sites.note: Two launches: Horse faces west, Laguna faces east over the desert. Each is scored on its own and the better one is shown.

sites.name: Otay Mesa
sites.note: Near the border; XC goes north and east.

sites.name: Soboba
sites.note: Flight park on the San Jacinto front.

sites.name: Santa Barbara (Skyport)
sites.note: South-facing front range above Santa Barbara. Sundowners and other north winds are over the back.
